lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abdul Quadir Talukder with Mr. Jafar Ali, Advocate ------ For the petitioners
Mr. Abdul Quddus Miah with Mr. Ranajit Kumar Dhar, Advocate ------ For the opposite parties
parties:
Hasan Raja Patwary and others
Vs.
Mohammad Reja Alias Mohammad Raja Patwary and others
full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 31.01.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 35 of 2006 reversing the judgment dated 23.03.2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Faridganj, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 37 of 2004 dismissing the suit, should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted a suit for declaration that the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 is illegal, fraud and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending, inter-alia, that late Mia Raja Patwary was the owner of suit property. The plaintiffs are the sons of late Hamid Raja Patwary who was the brother of late Mia Raja Patwary. The petitioners who are the defendant Nos. 1-6 are the sons and daughters of late Ali Raja Patwary and late Mia Raja Patwary had no male issue and he had two daughter defendant Nos. 7 and 8. Late Mia Raja Patwary having no male issue, he made gift of the property as described in the schedule of deed No. 6478 dated 23.09.1980 in favour of plaintiffs Nos. 1 and 2 and their brothers Siddique Raja and Sultan Ahmed Patwary. The plaintiffs and their brothers are in possession of the suit property. Late Mia Raja said the property in favour of plaintiffs vide deed No, 945 dated 31.01.1981. Late Mia Raja sold rest of the properties to different persons through different sale deeds. Plaintiffs obtained properties through gift made by late Mia Raja Patwary and purchase from him and as heirs of his father. Late Mia Raja having no male issue lived in the house of plaintiff No. 2 and died therein. Late All Reza Patwary, crated the bainanama by taking recourse fraud on the basis of the bainanama who filed Suit No. 48 of 1981 and obtained a sole decree and decreed plaintiffs came to know of this decree after obtaining a certified copy of the same and became clear to them that late All Rem obtained the impugned decree without taking deposition of late Mia Reza Patwary. The predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-6 obtained the impugned decree by creating forged bainanama. The plaintiffs were not aware of the decree of Suit No. 48 of 1981. There was salish on 02.01.2004 on the suit property. Subsequently on 10.01.2004 plaintiffs obtained copy of the suit register and on 01.03.2004 they obtained a certified copy of the Judgment and decree and cause of action arose from that date. Hence the suit.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that late Mia Raja Patwary ex-owner of the suit property when proposed to sell the suit property, the predecessor of present defendant agreed to purchase the same and total- consideration money of the suit property was fixed at Tk. 7000/- and out of total consideration money, late Mia Raja Patwary received Tk. 3000/- on 19.4.1978 and executed the bainanama. It was stipulated therein that Mia Raja Patwary would execute and register the sale on receipt of the balance consideration money of Tic. 4000/, But Mia Raja Patwary refused to execute and register the sale deed even after receipt of the entire consideration money. The predecessor of the present petitioners was, therefore, compelled to file the suit for specific performance of contract being No. 48 of 1981 and obtained sole decree. In the decree, the deposition of Ali Raja Patwary was recorded, Due to mistake the record of solenama was adjourned and instead the application for addition of party filed by the present plaintiff was fixed for hearing when the attention of the court was drawn to this, court found that it was on clerical mistake and the court vide order No. 15 dated 21.10.1981 vacated the order dated 27.08.1981 and decreed the suit on the basis of Solenama. The sale deed of the present plaintiff being a case of lispendense vide order No. 11 dated 04.06.1981 of the instant suit and the present plaintiffs having not filed any appeal against this order, the order dated 04.06.1981 stands valid and the present plaintiffs have not acquired any right to file the instant suit. Mia Raja Patwary defendant No.1 of Suit No. 48 of 1981 having admitted the bainanama and the court having decreed the suit on the basis of the bainanama, the plaintiffs have no right to claim that the bainanama is forged. In the decree of suit No. 48 of 1981 due to mistake of clerk, the boundaries of the suit property was not recorded and the clerical mistake can be corrected under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Sole decree cannot be unenforceable due to this mistake. The petitioners are in possession of the suit property. Mia Raja Patwary did not make gift of his property to anybody. The plaintiffs have created forged sale deed. The petitioners, therefore, pray for dismissal of the suit.

4. At the trial, the plaintiffs examined 4(four) witnesses and the defendants examined 3(three) witnesses in support of their respective cases.

5. The learned judge of the trial on conclusion of trial after hearing the parties, considering the evidence and other materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 23.03.2006. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred appeal before the learned District Judge, Chandpur. On transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, who after hearing the parties and considering the materials on record allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 31.01.2008.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendants as petitioners moved this court and obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr. Md. Abdul Quadir Talukder, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below and submits that the suit is barred by law and there is no cause of action to file this suit. He submits that Mia Raja Patwary was judgment-debtor in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 neither MM Raja Patwary or his legal heirs preferred any appeal against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 and as such judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 is binding for all. He also submits that the plaintiffs did not take possession of the suit land on the basis of alleged deed being number 945 dated 31.10.1981 and as such the deed has not been acted upon. He further submits that the suit is not maintainable without prayer for recovery of khas possession. He submits that impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal as per Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and such the judgment and decree is not sustainable in law. He lastly submits that the learned Judge of the appellate court has traveled beyond the pleadings of the plaintiffs and he prayed for to make the rule absolute.

8. Mr. Abdul Quddus Miah, the learned advocate appearing for the opposite parties opposed the rule and submits that the defendants (defendants in present suit and plaintiff in earlier suit) failed to prove by any evidence that Dulal Raja Patwary and Mia Raja Patwary filed any application for addition of party under order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981. He submits that Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 was filed on 21.01.1981 for Specific Performance of Contract to enforce the Bainapatra dated 19.04.1978. The present plaintiff purchased the suit land on 21,12.1980 earlier filing of suit in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 and as such the present plaintiffs were necessary parties to the suit under section 27(b) of the Specific Performance of Contract Act. He submits that had the decree is genuine one the plaintiffs definitely would try to get the Kabala but there is no Kabala for the last 23 years after decree. He further submits that exhibit-I certified copy of the suit register filed by the plaintiff in earlier suit shows that the suit being number Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 was dismissed which is findings of the court of appeal below in judgment at page 10 (running page 38). He also submits that the document of solenama is fraudulent since Mia Raja Patwary put his signature in English in the solenama. He further submits that the decree dated 29.10.1981 does not contends any schedule of land. He lastly submits that the appellate court being last and final court of facts rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and no reason is called for to interfere by this court in revision since there is no misreading and non-considerations of the materials evidence on record and he prayed for discharged the rule. In support of his contention he has referred the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 294.

9. In order to appreciate the submissions made by the learned advocates for the parties, I have gone through the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below very carefully.

10. Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the court of appeal below has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

11. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiffs brought a suit for declaration that judgment and decree obtained in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 is illegal, fraud and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 was filed by Md. Ali Raja Patwary the predecessors of the defendant-petitioners for Specific Performance of Contract against Mia Raja Patwary and others which was decreed on compromise on 26.10,1981. On the other hand, the plaintiffs in the instant suit claimed that they purchased the suit land on 21.12.1980 from the defendants of earlier Title Suit No. 48 of 1981.

<u>12. On perusal of the judgment and decree of the trial court it appears that the learned Judge of the trial court dismissed the suit on the ground of barred by limitation since the present plaintiffs earlier filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party in Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 which was rejected with the findings-“বাদীপক্ষ দেঃ ৪৮/৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার বিগত ইং ২৬/১০/১৯৮১ তারিখের রায় ও বিগত ২৯/১০/১৯৮১ ইং তারিখের প্রচারিত ডিক্রিকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করিয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করিয়াছেন বিগত ইং ২৭/৪/২০০৪ তারিখ। বাদীপক্ষের দাখিলী বিগত ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার প্রচারিত আদেশ সমূহ হইতে দেখা যায় যে, (প্রঃচিঃ-১) অত্র মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ মোঃ রাজা পাটওয়ারী ও দুলাল রাজা পাটওয়ারী ঐ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার পক্ষভূক্ত হওয়ার জন্য পক্ষভূক্তির দরখাস্ত আনয়ন করেন এবং পক্ষভূক্তির এরূপদরখাস্ত সরাসরি না মঞ্জুর হয় বিগত ইং ৪/৬/১৯৮১ তারিখে। নামঞ্জরের আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে দরখাস্তকারীগণ অর্থাত বর্তমান মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করিয়া উচ্চতর আদালতে গমন করেন নাই। বর্তমান বাদী পক্ষের দেঃ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার পক্ষভূক্তির জন্য আনীত দরখাস্ত নামঞ্জুর হওয়ায় ইহা আদালতের নিকট সহজেই প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বর্তমান বাদীপক্ষ দেঃ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দামার বিষয় সম্পর্কে এবং ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার রায় ডিক্রি সম্পূর্ণরূপে জ্ঞাত ছিল। দেঃ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার রায় প্রচারিত হয় বিগত ইং ২৬/১০/৮১ তারিথে এবং ডিক্রি স্বাক্ষরিত হয় বিগত ইং ২৯/১০/৮১ তারিখে। দেঃ ৪৮/৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার রায় ডিক্রি ১৯৮১ সালে প্রচারিত হইলেও উহার বিরুদ্ধে বাদীপক্ষ সুদীর্ঘকাল অতিবাহিত হওয়ার পর কেন অত্র মোকদ্দমার আনয়ন করিয়াছেন তাহার কোন গ্রহনযোগ্য ব্যাখ্য্ বাদীপক্ষ উপস্থাপন করিতে সক্ষম হন নাই। বাদীপক্ষ ঐ দেঃ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমা সম্পূর্ন অবগত থাকিয়া উক্ত মোকদ্দামার পক্ষভূক্তির জন্য আবেদন করিয়াও উক্ত মোকদ্দমার প্রচারিত রায় ডিক্রি বিষয়ে বাদী পক্ষ জানিতেন না কিংবা জানিতে পারেন নাই বাদীপক্ষের এইরূপ কাহিনী আদালতের নিকট গ্রহনযোগ্য নহে এবং বাদীপক্ষের এইরূপ বক্তব্য বিশ্বাস করার কোন যৌক্তিক ও গ্রহনযোগ্য কারণ নাই বলিয়া আদালত মনে করে। যেহেতু বাদী পক্ষ নিজেরাই দেঃ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার পক্ষভূক্তির আবেদন করেছিল সেই হেতু এই বাদীপক্ষ ৪৮/১৯৮১ নং মোকদ্দমার প্রচারিত ২৬/১০/১৯৮১ ইং তারিখের রায় ও ডিক্রি ২৯/১০/১৯৮১ ইং তারিখের ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে সম্পূর্নরূপে অবগত ছিল বলিয়া স্পষ্টরূপে প্রতীয়মান হয় এবং ২৬/১০/১৯৮১ ইং তারিখের রায় ও ২৯/১০/১৯৮১ এং তারিখের প্রচারিত ডিক্রির বিষয়ে বাদীপক্ষ ১৯৮১ সালেই সম্পূর্নরূপে জ্ঞান থাকিয়া তামাদির নির্দিষ্ট মেয়াদের মধ্যে অত্র মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন না করায় অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি গুরুতর তামাদি দোষে বারিত করিয়া আদালতের নিকট প্রমানিত হয়।”</u>

<u>13. The learned Judge of the appellate court allowed the appeal and reversed the decisions of the trial court. To answer the submissions of the learned advocate for the opposite parties that exhibit-1 certified copy of the suit register filed by the plaintiffs in earlier suit shows that the Title Suit No. 48 of 1981 was dismissed findings of the court of appeal in the judgment. In order to appreciate this submissions, 1 have gone through the relevant portion of the judgment and exhibit-1 it appears that the findings of the learned Judge of the appellate court is misreading and non-considerations which clearly shows that the application filed by the present plaintiff under order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected vide order 11 dated 04.06.1981 and suit was ordered that the suit be decreed on compromise in terms of solenama which do part of the decree.</u>

<u>14. On perusal of the exhibit-1 it further appears that the present plaintiff earlier filed an application under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party which was rejected and thereafter they did not take any step to the higher forum against the said order. Moreso, they have filed the instant suit after long 23 years of time and as such the learned Judge of the trial court has rightly dismissed the suit on the ground that suit is barred by limitation.</u>

15. By now it is settled that the appellate court being last and final court of that will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. In case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate court to reassess the evidence to arrive at his own independent finding. The findings of the trial court should not be easily disturbed as a matter of course and before reversing the findings and decisions of the trial court the appellate court should think twice or more than twice. In the instant case, I am of the view that specific findings of the trial court have not been reversed by the appellate court exercising its power which is mandatory provisions of law under Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This view find support in the case of Hajarilal Mondal and others Vs. Md. Mozaffor Bepari and others, reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77, wherein their lordship held:

"In is a settled principle of law that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. In case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. In the instant case we find that the specific findings of the trial court have not been reversed by the lower appellate court exercising its power under Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure."

16. I have gone through the decision cited by the learned advocate for the opposite party reported in 17 BLD (AD) 294. I am respectful agreement with the principles enunciated therein. But the facts leading to that case is quite distinguishable to that of the instant case and therefore, to that effect I am also unable to accept his submissions.

17. In view of the discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I am of the view that the judgment 'and decree passed by the lower appellate court cannot be sustained in law and are liable to be set aside. Thus, I find merit in the rule.

18. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 31.01.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 35 of 2006 are set aside and those of the trial court are restored and affirmed. However, there will be no order as to costs.

19. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

20. Let the Lower Court Records along with a copy of the judgment be sent to the court concerned at once.

End.
